meta.title: The C Form: Three on Every String
meta.summary: The C form is the only CAGED window this chapter fills in evenly, and its six open strings turn out to give you five of the seven degrees, including the note chapter 3 had to leave out.

spans.text: means string 5, fret 3 — string first, then fret, the shorthand you've been reading since chapter 1's closer. The C form sits at barre fret

Eighteen dots — the most of any window in this chapter — and three on every single string, with nothing left short. Of the five windows, the C form is the only one that comes out even like this. And it needs no stretch to hold: settle your fretting fingers over frets 1 through 4 and every fretted dot in the window is already under one of them, with the open strings ringing underneath for free.

Eighteen dots sounds like a lot to keep straight, but six of them cost nothing to reach — they're the open strings. The window's real news is the other twelve: the same eight chord tones and four pentatonic notes you already knew from earlier chapters, plus the six new dots that just arrived.

Same window, four layers deep now. Chapter 1 lit two roots here, chapter 2 lit eight chord tones, chapter 3 lit twelve. This lesson lights all eighteen — the window is complete, and the shape underneath it hasn't changed since the first time you saw it.
